subject: Streaming sentinel: header mismatch causing intermittent checkout stalls
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@pointcommerce.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: PointCommerce Ops <oncall@pointcommerce.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Checkout stalls / high p99 during streaming ingress

Hi Sean,

We've started seeing intermittent checkout stalls this morning in production (eu-west and us-west regions). P99 latency for the live streaming call to Redwood jumped from ~220ms to >3.5s, and ~2.7% of requests returned a 502-like parse error from our client-side adapter.

Attached is a short log snippet and a small trace showing repeated "parser: sentinel not found" messages and header truncation around the chunk boundary. Our frontend team says the issue correlates with customers using the streaming client (chunked upload of cart metadata).

Can the Redwood team triage? This is impacting a subset of checkout traffic (roughly 10% of sessions) — happy to give access to a replay environment.

Attachments: [client-log-20270614.txt], [trace-snippet.json]

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
SRE, PointCommerce

Subject: Re: Checkout stalls / high p99 during streaming ingress

Hi Alex — thanks for the signal and the attachments. I've looped in Marissa (CS lead) and Ben (AE) so we can coordinate, and Grace to flag if this needs exec visibility.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you confirm whether the affected clients are on the JS SDK (v1.8.2) or a custom adapter?
- If you can reproduce in a staging replay, please mark the replay link and share the time window.

Short mitigation options to try right away (low-risk):
- Force non-streaming fallback for the checkout path (disable chunked streaming) — we expect this will avoid the parser path that is failing.
- If you can't fallback, try increasing chunk_size to 64KB as a temporary experiment.

We will open a priority ticket (INF-4321) and start triage on our side. I'll confirm the on-call SLA and an ETA for a patch once we have an initial repro.

Sean
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@pointcommerce.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-14T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout stalls / high p99 during streaming ingress

Alex — quick update from triage: our runtime team reproduced a parsing fault when the client sent an additional sentinel header in the same chunk that also contained a small trailer block. The streaming parser currently treats the sentinel as a strict header delimiter; if the header boundary is split across frames the parser can drop the trailing header bytes and subsequently mis-interpret the next chunk as a payload boundary, which manifests as increased parse errors and stalled responses.

Key notes:
- Repro was against SDK v1.8.2 with chunk_size=32KB and a specific metadata payload pattern (customer-supplied metadata with a very long attribute).
- This is not affecting non-streaming calls.
- We've attached a short trace that shows header bytes truncated at the frame boundary (trace-snippet.json).

Planned actions:
1) Hotfix: change parser to be tolerant of split sentinel across frames (canary patch within 24–36 hours).
2) Medium: publish SDK advisory that recommends chunk_size >= 64KB or fallback to non-streaming for affected checkout flow.
3) Long-term: add unit coverage for sentinel-splitting and enhance logging to surface the exact byte offsets.

Workarounds for you to try now:
- Disable streaming on checkout (preferred immediate mitigation).
- If disabling is not feasible, set chunk_size to 64KB and report back whether error rate drops.

I've filed INF-4321 and assigned P0; engineering will post updates in the Jira ticket. We'll also prepare a short exec-ready incident note if the customer requests credits or an SLA exception.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex@pointcommerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout stalls / high p99 during streaming ingress

Marissa — appreciate the quick reproduction and the mitigation plan. We rolled the non-streaming fallback for the most critical checkout flow at 15:30 PT and saw p99 return to ~240ms within 10 minutes; error rate dropped to baseline.

Two asks from PointCommerce:
1) ETA for the canary patch (we need at least a canary in us-west within 48 hours if possible).
2) Given the customer impact, can we get a credit/incident concession while we coordinate? Our finance team will need a short incident summary for our audit.

Attaching a screenshot of our monitoring alert and an extended log slice for the replay (screenshot-headers.png, client-log-20270614.txt).

Thanks — will monitor INF-4321 and await updates.

— Alex
SRE, PointCommerce
